messages:
Maya: heads-up — CI alerted a perf regression on the latest release gate (PR #8421). p95 token latency up ~25% for short sequences when batching enabled. Anyone already looking?

CI Bot: perf-checker: regression detected on playground-inference-smoke (commit 9f3b2d7 -> 1.2.0-rc.7). Metric: p95_tokens_latency short_seq (seq=32) increased from 85ms -> 110ms (+29%). See: https://ci.redwood.example/perf/8421

Josh: thanks, digging in. quick question — does CI repro use the new batching heuristic that switches to groupBySize?

Anita: yes CI uses latest runtime image built from PR.8421 (changes to batching heuristics + kernel selection tie-break). I ran a local run and saw similar numbers but need a clean repro.

Tom: possible candidate: change in batch splitting when sequence < 64 — we started grouping by token count which may be preventing efficient kernel selection.

Rachel: can someone run a targeted bisect? I can do local git bisect if we have a fast perf test.

Maya: I started a local perf script: `./scripts/perf_seq_latency.sh --model=redwood-7b --seq=32 --iters=50 --batch=8`. On main before PR it reports ~82ms p95. After current head it's ~108ms.

Josh: cool. I'll try `git bisect` on the runtime repo. Suggested workflow: `git bisect start HEAD v1.2.0-rc.6` then `git bisect run ./perf-bisect.sh` where perf-bisect.sh exits 0 for good (<=90ms) and 1 for bad (>100ms).

Anita: small note — perf-bisect.sh should set NUM_WARMUP=10 and use `--no-telemetry` to avoid noise. Also pin CPU governor to performance on CI machine to be deterministic.

Tom: running bisect now on a beefy devbox, will post results. (running `git bisect run`...)

Tom: halfway update — bisect narrowed it down to a small range 9f3b2d7..c1a7d55. Looks like the change that added "prefer_token_grouping" in batching policy is suspicious.

Rachel: can you dump the scheduler decisions log from that commit? `RUNTIME_LOG=batching=debug ./start_runtime` and repro a run. Need to see if it's choosing smaller micro-batches that force slower kernels.

Tom: pasted excerpt: `batching: selected_groups=[4,4] prefer_token_grouping=true kernel_hint=matmul_small` then later `kernel_selector: fallback -> matmul_generic (slower) due to shape mismatch`. That fallback looks correlated.

Josh: aha — prefer_token_grouping combined with tie-breaker change causes shapes that miss optimized matmul kernel cache. We introduced the tie-breaker in PR 8349 to prefer memory-friendly shapes, but didn't update kernel keys.

Maya: so repro steps to verify: checkout commit c1a7d55 (bad), run `./scripts/perf_seq_latency.sh --model=redwood-7b --seq=32 --batch=8` and capture `kernel_selector.log`. Compare to v1.2.0-rc.6 where it picks `matmul_fast` vs `matmul_generic` on bad.

Anita: I ran that and confirmed. On good commit: `matmul_fast` used, p95=83ms. On bad commit: `matmul_generic` used, p95=112ms.

Rachel: proposed fix: revert the tie-breaker change in the batching policy and add a kernel-key normalization step so shape variants map to the same optimized kernel. Can we do a quick patch and run CI perf?

Josh: I'll open PR that reverts the tie-breaker and adds kernel-key normalization unit test + a small perf run in CI. Marking this a rollout-blocker until perf numbers return to baseline.

CI Bot: perf-checker: triggered perf job for PR #8437 (contains revert + kernel-key normalization). Running targeted perf suite.

Maya: thanks everyone. Once CI confirms, we'll proceed with a hotfix revert to release channel. For now, don't merge unrelated batching changes. :thumbsup:

Tom: FYI local bisect log saved to /tmp/bisect-1761154320.log if anyone needs it.

Anita: follow-up — we should add a small regression test in the nightly suite to cover seq=32 batch=8 path to prevent future silent kernel-selection regressions.

Rachel: agreed. I'll add the test after PR lands.

Maya: closing the loop when CI finishes. Thanks all.
